newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand streamlines key economic data releases.
newsitem.headline: Thailand streamlines key economic data releases.

text.p: Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday that Thailand would streamline the way it will release economic data to reduce chances of giving wrong signals to financial and stock markets.

Amnuay told reporters after meeting top finance ministry and central bank officials that a high-level, multi-agency committee would handle screening and announcement of key economic indicators in the future.
It would be chaired by Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi, deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand, he said.

"The committee will aim at providing more complete and comprehensive information. Up until now, the markets sometimes have problems interpreting diverse data from different government agencies," he said.

The minister said the committee, comprising representatives of the central bank, finance ministry, budget bureau and commerce ministry, will brief a team of economists from Moody's Investors Service which will arrive in early March to review the Thai economy.
Moody's said late last week it will review for possible downgrade Thailand's long-term sovereign debts.
Moody's said on Friday it might cut Thailand's A2 long-term foreign currency debt and deposit ratings.
It said the review was prompted by concerns over the soundness of Thailand's financial sector as well as over constraints on macroeconomic policy-making.
